commands.name: status
commands.description: Read-only snapshot: onboarding health, phase, gates, handoff, cell counts, reservations, active workers, decisions, staleness warnings, recommended next step. `lanes` is summarized by default: the ACTIVE lane (the one this session is bound to) in full, plus counts-by-phase and bare ids for every other lane record — pass --lanes-full for the full per-lane array. `workers` is a derived view — live-heartbeat sessions joined with their current cell claim — never state.json's hand-mutated `workers` array. `cells.archivable` is the retirement backlog — {features, cells, ids} for features whose cells are ALL terminal and which are therefore parsed on every call for nothing. `bee close` retires what it closes, so this only ever counts work that never went through close; the text report names it once it is worth a command.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of the text report.

lanes-full.description: Restore the `lanes` field to its full per-lane array (every lane record in full, including bound_sessions) instead of the default summary ({active, counts, ids}). Payload-size only — every other top-level field (phase/mode/feature/gates/cells/recommended_next/...) is unaffected either way.

brief.description: Fast orientation path for worker startup. Reads ONLY the state layer (state.json + config-derived gate_bypass_level/ship_visibility) — no cell scan, no review/handoff resolution, no models/tier_mix. Emits exactly {phase, feature, mode, gates, gate_bypass_level, ship_visibility, route} (route null when absent); ignored together with --lanes-full (mutually exclusive fast/full paths — --brief wins). Full `status` (this flag omitted) is unchanged.

commands.name: orient
commands.description: Session-start context packet: where the work is ({phase, feature, mode, gates, gate_bypass_level}), the decisions in force (active count, up to 3 recent one-liners, the feature's CONTEXT.md path when one exists on disk), the work state (open/claimed/capped counts, up to 5 ready cell ids, blockers), and exactly one recommended next step ({action, skill, command}) — the skill to load for the current phase, and a runnable command when the action names one (null otherwise). Reshapes the same snapshot `bee status` builds, plus ONE write of its own (sweep-at-every-door D1/D6): before the report is built, it resolves its own caller session and releases any OTHER session's expired, heartbeat-stale claim, parking that claim's cell `blocked` and naming the dead session and its worktree in the reason — the SAME sweep `bee cells claim-next` already runs, reached from a second door. When orient cannot resolve its own caller session it writes nothing and reports the count of expired claims it detected instead. `bee status` runs no such sweep and stays read-only.

json.description: Emit the machine-readable packet ({where, decisions, work, next}) instead of the six-line text summary.

commands.name: route
commands.description: Flow spelling of `bee state route`: read or record the route for the active feature — {class, lane, flags[], product_files}. Identical behaviour, flags and output; this is the name the lifecycle uses, so a caller never has to know the route lives under the `state` group.

set.description: Write mode: record a new route (requires --class/--lane/--flags/--files).

show.description: Read-only mode: print the currently recorded route (null when absent).

lane.description: Route lane (the triage lane classification — never a feature-routing flag).

flags.description: Comma-separated triage flag names; the empty string means zero flags.

files.description: Non-negative integer: the triage product-file count.

rationale.description: Optional free-text rationale for the route.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a one-line confirmation.

commands.name: shape
commands.description: Flow spelling of `bee intent set`: write the shaping anchor — the user's VERBATIM request plus what "done" means — before any code is touched. Identical behaviour, flags and output; shaping's whole output IS this anchor, so it carries the lifecycle's name.

request.description: The user's request, VERBATIM — their own words, never a paraphrase or a summary.

acceptance.description: What "done" means — the drift detector the anchor is checked against.

next-action.description: The single next step; the only field `intent advance` may move.

feature.description: Override the anchor key/feature instead of resolving the active feature from state.

cell.description: Cell id currently in flight (context only).

session.description: Session id to key on when there is no active feature.

do-not-reverse.description: Comma-separated decisions that must not be reversed.

stop-conditions.description: Comma-separated conditions under which the agent must stop and ask.

force.description: Pass "true" to replace a live anchor whose request/acceptance differ — a deliberate new objective, never a drift. Takes an explicit true/false value, same as cells.verify --passed.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a one-line confirmation.

examples: bee shape --request "example verbatim request" --acceptance "example acceptance criteria" --next-action "example next step" --json

commands.name: gate

commands.name: cells.add
commands.description: Add a cell (or a whole-slice JSON array) from stdin, or from a JSON file. Exactly one of --file / --stdin is required at call time (both satisfy the schema; the handler itself enforces the choice).

commands.name: cells.claim
commands.description: Claim an open, dep-free cell for a worker. Refuses while Gate 2's execution component is unapproved or deps are uncapped. Backed by the same O_EXCL claim file claim-next uses (the claim-file store, acquired before the cell JSON flips) — a losing concurrent claimant gets a typed CLAIMED refusal naming the owner + expiry instead of silently double-owning the cell. --session-id is optional — resolves from CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID when omitted, and falls back to a legal sessionless claim when neither is present (single-session use is unaffected).

session-id.description: Claiming session identity (the claim-file store). Optional — resolves from CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, then falls back to a sessionless claim.

isolate.description: Route this claim through the write-policy isolate-create path (a fresh worktree) instead of claiming directly in this checkout. Only meaningful when the write-policy mode actually enforces isolation.

fix-first.description: Escape a red last-recorded test run (D2: no claim on a red base) and claim anyway. The reason is stored on the claim's own trace.fix_first.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a one-line confirmation.

commands.name: cells.cap
commands.description: Cap a cell (plumbing — `cells finish` is the porcelain completion verb and wraps this same door). A cap is commit-only proof: no test command runs here. Tests prove at the boundary — `bee close` runs commands.test when the feature has no worktree, `bee worktree merge` runs it when it does; CI runs the same command on every push. A repo with commands.test declared in .bee/config.json records {tests: 'boundary'} on the trace; no commands.test declared records {tests: 'undeclared'}. Small+ lanes still require non-empty --files (what the worker touched); high-risk still requires --outcome; a NEEDS_REVISION judge verdict still refuses without --override-judge.

deviations-file.description: Path to a deviations list (JSON array or newline-delimited text).

deviation.description: A single deviation line (one line, not a list) appended to trace.deviations at cap time — named-deviation prose that would otherwise never reach the pattern-candidate mining `bee knowledge promote` reads. Refused when the value is empty or whitespace-only. Repeat calls only keep the last occurrence (the flag parser is single-value, same as every other cells cap/finish flag); pass one line per invocation.

REQUIRED (D8): exactly five keys: outcome (non-empty string), commit (non-empty string), files (array), tests (a proof string "<command> — <result> — <scope reason>", three non-empty segments split on the first two " — " separators, e.g. "cargo test -p bee — green — touched close.rs"; a no-test-sentinel repo names the command segment "none"; a "red" result segment refuses the cap), deviations (array); an unknown or missing key refuses by name, as does a missing --report itself. Stored verbatim to trace.report.

friction.description: One-line friction note, only when a friction trigger fired.

override-judge.description: Audited override reason — required to cap a cell whose latest semantic-judge verdict is NEEDS_REVISION (refused otherwise with JUDGE_REWORK_REQUIRED); recorded to trace.judge_overrides and logged as a decision.

session-id.description: Acting session identity, for the claim-ownership guard. Optional — resolves from CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID when omitted.

force-ownership.description: Override a live claim owned by a different session (audited).

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a one-line confirmation.

commands.name: cells.claim-next
commands.description: Cross-session selection + claim: sweeps stale claims (TTL expired AND heartbeat stale) in-pass first — this IS sweepExpiredClaims's production trigger — then picks the next open cell to claim: the acting session's own bound lane (or the default pipeline when unbound) first, ONLY when its execution gate is approved; empty or unapproved falls back to every OTHER pipeline whose OWN execution gate is approved (an unapproved lane is never touched), ordered by backlog rank then lane created_at. Cells whose files intersect another session's active reservation hold are skipped (the acting session's own holds never exclude a cell). Claims via the two-store sequence (the claim file first, then the cell record, unwound with a claim-file release on any claimCell throw). Refuses (non-zero exit) when nothing is claimable (NO_APPROVED_WORK), the claims-store race is lost (CLAIMED), or the session's lane binding is broken (LANE_INVALID/LANE_MISSING/LANE_CORRUPT). --session-id is not required at the schema level — omit it and it resolves from CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID instead; a session id is still functionally required (claim-next resolves the acting session's own lane from it), so a call with neither still refuses, just from the handler rather than arg validation.

commands.name: cells.reset-budget

Refuses (typed RESET_NOT_NEEDED) unless the cell is actually budget-blocked, and refuses without an actor (--operator, or the BEE_AGENT_NAME env fallback). Requires --reason (audited), logs a decision BEFORE writing the cell (the audit survives even if the write itself fails), and appends {reset_at, reason, by_session, by_actor} to the append-only trace.budget_resets — never rewrites or drops any trace.attempts ledger entry. gate_bypass never substitutes for this: the budget check itself never reads bypass config, so this verb is the only reopening path at any bypass level.

reason.description: Why a retry is warranted — required, logged to the decision log.

session-id.description: Resetting session identity, recorded as by_session. Optional — resolves from CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID when omitted.

commands.name: cells.archive
commands.description: Move a fully-terminal feature's cells (every cell capped or dropped — refuses naming any open/claimed cell) out of the hot .bee/cells/ scan path into .bee/cells/archive/<feature>/, and record its capped/dropped counts in the archive summary ledger so `bee status` reports an honest archived total without scanning the archive tree. Refuses when --feature is the active state.feature (archiving in-flight work is never legal) or when the feature has zero cells. --all-but-active sweeps instead of naming one feature: every feature whose active cells are ALL capped/dropped is archived in one call, the active feature and any feature still holding a live cell are kept and NAMED in `skipped` with the reason. It refuses outright when state.feature is empty — with no resolvable active feature "all but active" would degrade into "all" and archive the in-flight work. Exactly one of --feature / --all-but-active. This is the pressure valve for the hot read path: `bee status` and `bee orient` parse every file in .bee/cells/ on every call, so a repo that never retires finished features pays a growing tax on every orientation.

Optional --kind is 'intent' or 'lease' (default 'lease'): 'lease' is a worker's own write-time reservation and stays a hard conflict; 'intent' declares a broad/glob planning-time scope that the write guard only warns about (never hard-blocks) unless it collapses onto the exact write target.

commands.name: decisions.log
commands.description: Append a decision event to the append-only decision log. Rejects secret-shaped or instruction-like content. Once docs/decisions/taxonomy.json exists, a zero-tag event is refused (typed, names --tags); without that file it warns and proceeds. --relation is required on every call: supersedes:<id>[,...] retires earlier decide/supersede events (resolved against the currently active set, same as decisions supersede's target), touches:<id>[,...] notes a related decision without retiring it, or none when this decision relates to nothing active. A missing or malformed --relation refuses, naming up to 3 conflict candidates and the fix. Decision text that reads as an inline supersession ("supersede(s|d)"/"replaces"/"overrides"/"no longer applies"/"instead of the previous") is refused unless --relation supersedes:<id> names the earlier decision, or `decisions supersede` is used instead. Decision text that reads as a deferral ("defer"/"for now"/"revisit when"/"revisit if"/"later") is refused unless --trigger names a registered trigger (see `triggers add`). Success output carries a `conflict_candidates` array (up to 3, ranked like `decisions search`'s --text scoring) naming active decisions that share a tag or score >=2 term hits with this one — warn-only, never a refusal; empty when none.

tags.description: Comma-separated lowercase slugs (e.g. "billing,nightly-job"), stored on the event for later --tag recall.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a one-line confirmation.

relation.description: Required. supersedes:<id>[,...] | touches:<id>[,...] | none — the decision's relation to prior ones. supersedes: retires the named decide/supersede event(s) from `decisions active`, the same as a `decisions supersede` target; touches: notes a related decision that stays active; none: relates to nothing active.

commands.name: decisions.archive

Refuses (typed) when zero events qualify. Use `decisions active --all` / `decisions search --all` to keep reaching archived events afterward.

commands.name: decisions.tag
commands.description: Append a retro-tag event that overlays tags/scope onto an existing decide/supersede event WITHOUT rewriting its jsonl line — visible via `decisions active`/`decisions search` (including --all) at read time. --target accepts a full id or a unique short8 prefix. --stdin accepts a JSON array of {target, tags, scope?} for a batch: every entry is validated before any write, and one unresolvable target refuses the WHOLE batch (nothing appended). The latest tag event wins when several target the same decision; overlay REPLACES the whole tags array, and scope only when the tag event carries one.

target.description: Full id or short8 prefix of the decide/supersede event to tag. Required unless --stdin is set.

tags.description: Comma-separated lowercase slugs (e.g. "billing,nightly-job"). Required (unless --stdin) — replaces the target's effective tags entirely.

scope.description: Optional scope to overlay onto the target. Omit to leave the target's existing scope untouched.

stdin.description: Read a JSON array of {target, tags, scope?} from stdin for a batch retro-tag (all-or-nothing).

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a one-line confirmation.

commands.name: decisions.render
commands.description: Render docs/decisions/index.md from the active decision store (overlay-aware): grouped by scope then tag (untagged last), newest-first inside each group, one line per decision "short8 · YYYY-MM-DD · first line of decision text". Superseded/redacted events are always excluded; a supersede event renders under its inherited scope/tags. Consumes the SAME overlay-applied read path as `decisions search`/`active`, so a retro-tagged legacy event renders under its overlaid scope/tags, never under "untagged". The file carries a provenance header and is deterministic (byte-identical for the same store) — it is regenerated only, never hand-edited.

all.description: Also reach events archived by `decisions archive` — same union-read flag as `decisions search`/`active`. Omit to render the active store only.

check.description: Read-only: compute the index and compare it byte-for-byte against docs/decisions/index.md on disk, without writing. Exits non-zero (and never writes) when the on-disk file is missing or has drifted (e.g. hand-edited) from what the store would render.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a one-line confirmation.

commands.name: state.set
commands.description: Set one or more top-level routing fields; only the flags given are written and every other field is preserved. Every call requires explicit --owner equal to the selected default/lane record's valid pre-mutation phase; missing/mismatched ownership or a corrupt phase refuses before write, and a successful phase change rolls ownership forward without persisting an owner field. --phase is validated against the known-phase enum AND against the tail guard: "compounding" is never settable directly (only `state scribing-run` produces it), and "compounding-complete" is legal only from "compounding", only with zero scribing debt, and only with a FRESH recorded compounding run (`state compounding-run`, matching feature, at >= last_scribing_run.at) — --waive-compounding permits the close without one, logging a decision. Every other transition, including all backward moves and --phase idle, stays permissive. Target resolution (symmetric with the read path): explicit --lane <feature> always wins > the calling session's bound lane when --lane is omitted (identity self-resolved at operation moment) > the default state.json for an unbound session. --no-lane forces the default record from a bound session. A missing or corrupt lane — explicit or session-bound — refuses loudly with zero writes, never a silent fall-back to the default. --feature is rejected whenever the selected target is a lane record.

feature.description: Feature slug to set. Rejected together with --lane.

owner.description: Selected record's exact pre-mutation phase. Required for every state set mutation; never persisted.

lane.description: Route the mutation to this lane record instead of the default state.json. Refuses if the lane is missing or corrupt. Omitted: the calling session's bound lane is targeted automatically; unbound sessions target the default record.

no-lane.description: Force the default state.json even when the calling session is bound to a lane. Cannot be combined with --lane.

waive-scribing-debt.description: Permit --phase compounding-complete while capped behavior_change cells are still unsynced to docs/specs/. Never silent: it logs a decision naming every waived cell.

waive-compounding.description: Permit --phase compounding-complete without a fresh recorded `state compounding-run` (matching the last scribing run, same feature). Never silent: it logs a decision naming the feature.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a one-line confirmation.

examples: bee state set --lane demo-lane --owner exploring --phase planning --json

commands.name: state.gate
commands.description: Approve or unapprove a named gate, OR pass --merge instead of --name to approve/unapprove the MERGED shape+execution gate in ONE call (sets approved_gates.shape AND approved_gates.execution together, since bee now asks a single Gate 2 question at the end of briefing in place of the separate shape and execution questions). --merge and --name are mutually exclusive. This dedicated command does not accept routing --owner. Idempotent: the same call run twice yields an identical file. Target resolution (symmetric with the read path): explicit --lane <feature> always wins > the calling session's bound lane when --lane is omitted > the default state.json for an unbound session. --no-lane forces the default record. A missing or corrupt lane — explicit or session-bound — refuses loudly with zero writes. A --merge approval inherits the SAME high-risk advisor-consult precondition that already guards a --name execution approval — refuses when mode is high-risk and advisor_ref is missing or stale, before any write. Under --merge, both gates carry the approved_for_plan_rev stamp (a plain --name execution approval still stamps execution alone), so a later `state plan-rev bump` revokes both instead of leaving the merged gate half-revoked.

name.description: Gate name. Required unless --merge is set; refused together with --merge.

merge.description: Approve/unapprove shape AND execution together in this one call, instead of a single named gate. Mutually exclusive with --name.

approved.description: Whether the gate(s) are approved ("true" or "false").

lane.description: Route the mutation to this lane record instead of the default state.json. Refuses if the lane is missing or corrupt. Omitted: the calling session's bound lane is targeted automatically; unbound sessions target the default record.

no-lane.description: Force the default state.json even when the calling session is bound to a lane. Cannot be combined with --lane.

owner.description: NOT accepted by this dedicated command — declared here only so the dispatcher's central unknown-flag check still lets it through to this handler's own specific refusal ("--owner is not accepted..."); routing ownership protects generic `state set` fields only.

actor.description: Who is approving — "user" (default) or "auto" for an approval made under gate_bypass. --actor auto requires BOTH --bypass-level and --reason so a bypassed approval is never less traceable than a stopped one.

bypass-level.description: The bypass level under which an --actor auto approval was made, mirroring gate_bypass's own vocabulary. Required when --actor auto is passed.

reason.description: Why an --actor auto approval did not stop for the human gate. Required when --actor auto is passed.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a one-line confirmation.

examples: bee state gate --lane demo-lane --name execution --approved true --json

commands.name: state.waiting-on.set
commands.description: Mark the run as waiting on the human — the agent's own declaration that it asked a gate-shaped or freeform question and is now blocked on an answer (D1: run_state reads "awaiting-approval" from this mark exactly like it does from a pending gate). Writes the mark on the live workflow record when a feature is currently active (the calling session's bound lane, or the default record's own feature) and rebuilds that feature's lane/state projections so `bee status` reflects it immediately; with no feature active, writes the SESSION-SCOPED mark directly on the default .bee/state.json record instead (D3 — a question asked before any feature exists still needs a home). The mark carries --kind, --subject, and the resolved owning session (D4's stale-expiry heartbeat check reclaims against it). It ends three ways, none of them this command: the human's next message clears it automatically, `bee state waiting-on clear` clears it explicitly, or it expires once its own age AND its owning session's heartbeat have both gone stale.

kind.description: What is being waited on — a formal gate, or a question the agent asked.

subject.description: The gate name or the question text being waited on.

session-id.description: The session id to record as the mark's owner. Omitted: resolved the usual way (BEE_SESSION_ID/CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, then the single live session).

lane.description: Name the target workflow by its lane feature explicitly, instead of resolving it from the calling session or the default record. Refuses if it names no live workflow.

no-lane.description: Force the session-scoped default record even when a feature is live or the calling session is bound to a lane.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a one-line confirmation.

examples: bee state waiting-on set --kind question --subject "which approach?" --json
bee state waiting-on set --kind gate --subject execution --lane demo-lane --json

commands.name: state.waiting-on.clear
commands.description: Explicitly clear a live waiting-on-the-human mark (D2's agent-driven clearing path) — a no-op, never a refusal, when nothing is live. Targets the same live workflow record a `state waiting-on set` with the same routing flags would (the calling session's bound lane, or the default record's own feature) and rebuilds that feature's lane/state projections; with no feature active, clears the session-scoped mark on the default .bee/state.json record instead (D3). The other two ways a mark ends — the human's next message, and stale expiry — need no command at all.

session-id.description: The session id used only to resolve the calling session's bound lane when --lane is omitted.

lane.description: Name the target workflow by its lane feature explicitly, instead of resolving it from the calling session or the default record. Refuses if it names no live workflow.

no-lane.description: Force the session-scoped default record even when a feature is live or the calling session is bound to a lane.

commands.name: state.plan-rev.bump
commands.description: Bump a workflow's plan_rev by 1. plan_rev lives ONLY on the workflow record, so this verb targets a lane exactly like gate/set/scribing-run (explicit --lane > the calling session's bound lane) but REFUSES when resolution would land on the default (non-lane) record — that record's workflow is not yet kept in sync. The bump immediately rebuilds the lane's projection: any gate stamped with the PRE-bump plan_rev (the execution gate always; the shape gate too when it was approved via `state gate --merge`) now projects as unapproved in .bee/lanes/<feature>.json, so a subsequent `cells claim` against that lane's cells refuses right away. Never touches any other workflow's record — context/review on THIS workflow are also untouched (they are never rev-stamped, so they stay effective across a bump).

lane.description: Route the bump to this lane's workflow record. Refuses if the lane is missing/corrupt, or names no live workflow record. Omitted: the calling session's bound lane is targeted automatically.

no-lane.description: Force default-record resolution — always refused (plan_rev is not yet default-path-synced). Named so the refusal is explicit rather than a silent fallback.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a one-line confirmation.

commands.name: state.route
commands.description: A validated route record — {class, lane, flags[], product_files, rationale, updated_at} — persisted on the ACTIVE feature's tracked record (session-bound lane when the calling session is bound, else the default record; refuses when no active feature). This verb never accepts a --lane TARGETING flag (unlike state set/gate/scribing-run) — --lane here is the route's OWN lane-classification value, not a feature router; targeting a non-active feature is not yet supported. --set requires --class (enum: feature/bugfix/docs/refactor/research/release/spike), --lane (enum: docs/tiny/small/spike/standard/high-risk), --flags (comma-separated; every entry must be one of the canonical triage flag names auth/authorization/data-model/audit-security/external-systems/public-contracts/cross-platform/covered-contract-change/proof-weakening/multi-domain; the empty string means zero flags, not a missing flag), --files (a non-negative integer); optional --rationale. Any enum/shape violation is a typed refusal naming the bad value and the legal set — free prose is never accepted, and nothing is written on refusal. --show is read-only: prints the currently recorded route (null when absent) without requiring any --set flag. `cells claim` warns on stderr, never refuses, when the claimed cell's feature has no route yet.

show.description: Read-only mode: print the currently recorded route (null when absent).

flags.description: Comma-separated triage flag names; the empty string means zero flags.

commands.name: state.workflows.list
commands.description: Read-only listing of every workflow record under .bee/runtime/workflows/ — {id, feature, status, phase, created_at, ...the full record} per entry, sorted newest-created first. Never writes. `status` is one of active/paused/closed (the workflow store's STATUS_VALUES); MULTIPLE records can be status "active" at once (one per concurrently-running lane) — this verb is a plain inventory, not itself the pruning tool (see `state workflows close`).

commands.name: state.workflows.close
commands.description: Closes zombie/stale workflow records without hand-editing .bee/runtime/workflows/*/state.json. Requires EXACTLY ONE of three mutually exclusive modes: --feature <f> closes every live (non-closed) record whose feature equals <f>; --id <id> closes the single record with that id; --all-but-active closes every live record whose feature differs from the CALLING context's own active feature (the same session-bound-lane-else-default resolution `state route` uses), keeping that one. The currently active feature's record is NEVER closed by --feature or --all-but-active — only --id may name it explicitly, bypassing the protection on purpose. Refuses with a typed, zero-mutation error when a mode selects zero live records (already closed, unknown id, unknown feature, or nothing left besides the active feature). Prints the closed {id, feature} pairs on success.

feature.description: Close every live workflow record for this feature. Refused if this is the currently active feature (use --id instead).

id.description: Close the single live workflow record with this id, even if it is the currently active feature's record.

all-but-active.description: Close every live workflow record except the currently active feature's.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a one-line confirmation.

commands.name: state.start-feature
commands.description: Guarded atomic feature start: fails closed with zero mutations unless the workspace is clean (idle/terminal phase, no handoff/active workers/reservations/claimed or nonterminal prior cells); on success sets feature/mode/phase and resets all four gates. "Active workers" is a derived view — live-heartbeat sessions joined with their current cell claim, never a hand-maintained list — so --session-id names the calling session on EITHER path (default or --as-lane) so its own heartbeat never counts against itself; without --session-id every live session, including the caller's own if it has one, counts. Optional --as-lane starts the feature as a per-feature lane record (.bee/lanes/<feature>.json) beside the default pipeline instead of mutating state.json; --paths is a comma-separated list of intended file paths checked against other sessions' active claims/reservations before the lane starts (--as-lane only).

feature.description: New feature slug.

as-lane.description: Start this feature as a per-feature lane record instead of the default state.json.

session-id.description: Calling session id: excludes its own live heartbeat from the derived active-workers precondition on either path, and — only meaningful with --as-lane and --paths — excludes its own active holds from the declared-paths conflict check.

paths.description: Comma-separated declared file paths checked against other sessions' active claims/reservations before the lane starts (only meaningful with --as-lane).

isolate.description: Route this feature start through the write-policy isolate-create path (a fresh worktree) instead of starting directly in this checkout. Only meaningful when the write-policy mode actually enforces isolation.

commands.name: state.rebuild-projections

A no-op (authoritative:false in the JSON result) when zero workflow records exist anywhere yet, state.json has a live non-idle default feature, or a lane names no live workflow record — the legacy file is left exactly as it already was in every no-op case. Also unconditionally rebuilds .bee/reservations.json from the lease store's current active path leases — never gated on workflow records, always overwrites. Safe to run any time.

commands.name: state.handoff.write
commands.description: Write a handoff through the guarded writer. --kind is required and never guessed: 'pause' writes today's free-form fields (--cell/--files/--done/--remaining/--next-action/--feature/--phase/--mode, whichever apply) plus the kind — no new precondition, the same surface-and-wait record as always. 'planned-next' REFUSES (typed, zero mutation) unless --previous-cell is capped (the cap itself ran the declared commands.test) AND --next-cell already has a claim owned by --writer-session (the carried claim) — on success the record stores writer_session/previous_cell/next_cell alongside kind. When a workflow resolves (--lane names it, or the calling session/default record is bound to one), the record is written to that workflow's OWN mailbox (.bee/runtime/handoffs/<workflow-id>/<seq>.json, scoped by --target-role) instead of the single legacy .bee/HANDOFF.json — a repo with no workflow records keeps writing the legacy file, byte-identical to before.

writer-session.description: planned-next only: the writing session id, which must already own the claim on --next-cell.

previous-cell.description: planned-next only: the just-capped cell id (must have status capped — cells finish ran the declared tests before that cap).

next-cell.description: planned-next only: the next cell id, whose claim must already be owned by --writer-session.

cell.description: pause only: the cell mid-flight when the pause was written.

files.description: pause only: comma-separated files touched so far.

feature.description: Feature slug to record on the handoff.

phase.description: Phase to record on the handoff.

mode.description: Mode to record on the handoff.

lane.description: Name the target workflow by its lane feature explicitly, instead of resolving it from the calling session or the default record.

target-role.description: Scope this mailbox record to a role (e.g. "reviewer") so it never clobbers another role's open handoff for the same workflow. Omitted = the default/unscoped slot.

session-id.description: The writing session id used ONLY to resolve which workflow this call targets when --lane is omitted (never required — BEE_SESSION_ID/CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID resolve it the usual way otherwise).

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a one-line confirmation.

examples: bee state handoff write --kind pause --cell wip-1 --next-action "resume wip-1" --json
bee state handoff write --kind planned-next --writer-session sess-handoff-writer --previous-cell handoff-prev --next-cell handoff-next --json

commands.name: state.handoff.adopt
commands.description: Adopt a planned-next handoff's carried claim into --session-id: transfers ownership of the handoff's next_cell claim to the adopting session, then clears the handoff — clear-after-adopt with idempotent recovery, not a single cross-file transaction (a crash between the two steps self-heals on the next call via a benign self-adopt). Refuses (typed, non-zero exit) when there is no handoff, the handoff is not kind planned-next (pause handoffs are never adopted — surface and wait instead), or the underlying claim adopt fails — every refusal leaves both the claim and the handoff untouched. When a workflow resolves (--lane, or --session-id's own bound lane/default record), this adopts from that workflow's mailbox instead of the single legacy .bee/HANDOFF.json.

session-id.description: Adopting session id — also used to resolve which workflow to adopt from when --lane is omitted.

lane.description: Name the target workflow by its lane feature explicitly.

target-role.description: Adopt from this role's mailbox slot instead of the default/unscoped one.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a one-line confirmation.

commands.name: state.handoff.show
commands.description: Show the current handoff, if any, with kind normalized for display (a missing/unknown kind reads as "pause" — fail-safe). Reports "no handoff" when none exists. When a workflow resolves (--lane, or the calling --session-id/default record's own bound lane), shows that workflow's own mailbox instead of the single legacy .bee/HANDOFF.json.

lane.description: Name the target workflow by its lane feature explicitly.

target-role.description: Show this role's mailbox slot instead of the default/unscoped one.

session-id.description: Resolve which workflow to show via this session's bound lane, when --lane is omitted.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a one-line summary.

commands.name: state.advisor-ref.record
commands.description: Record an advisor consult onto the selected record's advisor_ref — the high-risk execution-gate precondition needs a state field AND a verb. The verb stamps the staleness anchors ITSELF — current feature, newest active decision id, and sha256 of that feature's plan.md — so anchors are never caller-supplied; the caller passes only --advisor (identity) and --digest-file (its first 500 chars are stored as digest_head for audit). Refuses when no feature is active (phase idle/compounding-complete or no feature). Target resolution (symmetric with the read path): explicit --lane <feature> always wins > the calling session's bound lane when --lane is omitted > the default state.json for an unbound session; --no-lane forces the default record. A lane target — explicit or session-bound — records with anchors bound to the lane's own feature and plan.md, leaving the default state.json untouched; a missing or corrupt lane refuses loudly with zero writes. There is no clear verb — staleness makes an old ref inert.

advisor.description: Advisor identity that was consulted (e.g. the configured advisor model or cli command label).

digest-file.description: Path to the captured advisor consult digest; its first 500 chars are stored as digest_head for audit.

lane.description: Route the record to this lane instead of the default state.json. Refuses if the lane is missing or corrupt. Omitted: the calling session's bound lane is targeted automatically; unbound sessions target the default record.

no-lane.description: Force the default state.json even when the calling session is bound to a lane. Cannot be combined with --lane.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a one-line confirmation.

examples: bee state advisor-ref record --advisor gpt-5.6-sol --digest-file consult.txt --json

commands.name: state.advisor-ref.show
commands.description: Show the selected record's advisor_ref, if any, with its live staleness verdict (stale + reason list) computed against the current feature, newest active decision id, plan.md sha256, and the last execution-gate revocation. A missing or malformed advisor_ref reads as "no advisor_ref recorded", never a crash. Optional --lane <feature> shows the lane record instead of the default state.json.

lane.description: Show this lane record instead of the default state.json.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a one-line summary.

commands.name: state.compact-log
commands.description: Append one compaction telemetry record via the compaction store's append path — the durable write every compaction surface (the PreCompact hook, the SessionStart resume hook) and this verb both call, so the log stays reachable by command on any runtime whose hook execution is unconfirmed. --event is 'precompact' or 'resume'; compact_index/cell_compact_count follow the counting rule — only precompact records are counted, and only a precompact record counts itself. A write failure never changes the exit code (fail-open, logged locally).

session-id.description: Session id the record is scoped to.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a one-line confirmation.

unavailable.reason: the manual compaction verbs were never ported off Node; the session hooks still read compaction state
unavailable.fix: `bee state handoff write` is the supported way to leave a clean stop before compaction

commands.name: state.compact-check
commands.description: Read-only integrity sweep for a session (the compaction integrity sweep): session record, lane binding, claimed-cell ownership, execution gate, dependency capping, reservation holds, and intent-anchor presence. REPORTS ONLY — it never repairs, releases, or blocks, and it exits non-zero ONLY on a usage error, never on a detected mismatch (a mismatch is reported data). The JSON output's checks[] always carries an `anchor_missing` entry naming the exact command the anchor nudge would name (ANCHOR_NUDGE_COMMAND), so the nudge stays reachable by command on a runtime that never executes a hook.

session-id.description: Session id to sweep.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a one-line summary.

unavailable.reason: the manual compaction verbs were never ported off Node; the session hooks still read compaction state
unavailable.fix: `bee state handoff write` is the supported way to leave a clean stop before compaction

commands.name: state.compact-capsule
commands.description: Render the compact capsule for a session (the compact-capsule builder) — the narrow orientation body a SessionStart with source=compact emits INSTEAD of the full startup preamble: the state-mismatch block, the onboarding-MISSING line, the HANDOFF block with its adoption-refusal reason, the gate-bypass banner, phase/mode/feature/lane, the claimed cell with its verify and dependency status, the first open gate, next_action, the recorded commands, the compaction survival count with its advisory, and a POINTER to the critical patterns, in that order. It NEVER renders the intent anchor — the hook owns that — and no byte of it varies with anchor presence. Read-only, and reachable by command on any runtime whose hook execution is unconfirmed.

session-id.description: Session id the capsule is rendered for.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of the rendered capsule text.

unavailable.reason: the manual compaction verbs were never ported off Node; the session hooks still read compaction state
unavailable.fix: `bee state handoff write` is the supported way to leave a clean stop before compaction

commands.name: backlog.add
commands.description: Validate then append one row to .bee/backlog.jsonl (the source the feedback digest collects from) — agents never hand-edit .bee state. --type must be a KIND_ALIASES key or an already-normalized NORMALIZED_KINDS value (the feedback kind table), --severity is P1|P2|P3, --layer is a free non-empty string <=40 chars (no allowlist), --title is required and <=200 chars. Any rejection leaves the file untouched. The row is always appended regardless of --queue-submit; only the auto-commit is gated: --queue-submit defaults false and must be passed explicitly for a human queue-submission (the caller is always the agent process, but the flag marks intent — a new item for the processing queue vs. the agent logging its own friction/debt/finding about its own session). With --queue-submit, a merge in progress is detected up front and the commit is skipped with commit_skipped_reason:"merge_in_progress" plus a visible warning suffix in the text output; every other commit failure stays a silent committed:false as before.

feature.description: Optional feature slug.

queue-submit.description: NOT BUILT INTO THIS BINARY: the scoped git auto-commit path was never ported off Node, and passing this flag now refuses the call by name without writing the row. Append the row without it and commit .bee/backlog.jsonl yourself. (Original meaning: human queue-submission for this row, default false — only when true did the scoped auto-commit run at all.)

commands.name: backlog.propose

The command stops at the proposal — it never auto-starts bee-shaping for the new item. --story is required, <=200 chars (stored as the PBI title); --cos (acceptance criteria) is required, <=2000 chars; --feature is optional and reports as "—" when omitted. Any validation rejection leaves the log untouched.

feature.description: Optional feature slug; reports as "—" when omitted.

commands.name: knowledge.check
commands.description: Validate the docs/knowledge/ OKF v0.1 bundle. The walk never leaves docs/knowledge/; a missing or empty bundle is OK. Two levels — OKF errors: missing/unparseable frontmatter on a non-reserved .md, empty/absent type, frontmatter in a non-root index.md, a root index.md carrying any key but okf_version, a log.md date heading that is not ISO 8601. Profile warnings: type outside the nine profile types, missing profile-required field, dangling required_context/supersedes target, duplicate bee.id, duplicate bee.authoritative_for, and a parse→re-emit byte mismatch (not_canonical — the round-trip guard against silent misparse). Exits non-zero only on OKF errors, or on any finding under --strict.

strict.description: Promote profile warnings to errors: any finding at all exits non-zero.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON ({okf:{errors},profile:{warnings},counts}) instead of one line per finding.

Byte-identical for identical bundle contents: path-sorted entries, LF endings, never a timestamp or any other wall-clock value. With --check, re-renders in memory and byte-compares against disk without writing: any drift (a stale or missing index) exits non-zero naming the file — the same freshness idiom as `bee decisions render --check`.

check.description: Read-only freshness check: exit non-zero naming each stale index instead of writing.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON ({written,count} or, with --check, {checked,stale,drift}) instead of a one-line summary.

Filters are exact matches: --type on the concept type, --lifecycle on bee.lifecycle, --area on membership in bee.areas. A concept with missing or unparseable frontmatter still rows (null fields) — hiding files is not this verb's job; grading them is `knowledge check`'s.

type.description: Keep only concepts whose type equals this value (e.g. bee.pattern).

lifecycle.description: Keep only concepts whose bee.lifecycle equals this value (draft|active|superseded|archived).

area.description: Keep only concepts whose bee.areas array contains this value.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON ({concepts,count}) instead of one row per line.

commands.name: knowledge.context
commands.description: Assemble the budget-aware context manifest for a work item. Resolves --work <id> to the bee.work-item concept whose bee.id matches, then ranks: (1) the work item, (2) its bee.plan sibling in the same work/<id>/ directory, (3) bee.required_context walked TRANSITIVELY in BFS depth order — an already selected path is skipped silently, so a cycle is deduped and never an error, and a dangling or out-of-bundle link is tolerated (OKF §5; grading it is `knowledge check`'s job), (4) the bee.critical: true concepts RANKED BY RELEVANCE to the work item and cut to the pinned keep, (5) every bee.decision concept whose bee.areas overlaps the work item's. The ranked list is then cut at --budget <tokens>: the first entry that would overshoot ends the manifest, and it plus every lower-ranked entry is named in `truncated`. Relevance is the IDF-weighted fraction of a concept's own distinctive vocabulary that the work item's text covers, over title/description/tags and body, plus a small tag/area bonus — chosen by measurement over the live bundle (AUC 0.805 against hand labels; tag overlap alone scored 0.550 and left 48 of 49 patterns tied at zero, so it is disqualified as the signal). The top few criticals are a FLOOR whose cost is reserved out of the budget left after rank 1, so a universal lesson is never evicted by a long required_context chain and the work item is never displaced by its own floor; --budget remains a hard ceiling. Nothing is dropped silently: every critical is accounted for exactly once across `entries` (whose reason names its score and rank), `truncated`, and `excluded` ({path, score, reason}), with `critical_total` stating the population. `zero_signal_count` is always reported, and a real population that is mostly zero FAILS with a typed zero_signal error — a ranking where most items tie at zero is a path sort wearing a relevance label. Ties break by path, so two runs are byte-identical. Sizes are estimated as bytes/4 and the output NAMES that estimator — bee vendors no tokenizer. The output is an ordered MANIFEST — per entry: repo-relative path, bytes, est_tokens, and a one-line inclusion reason — and NEVER file content; the agent decides what to read. `decisions` in the header is informational: the work item's own bee.decisions list, read from its frontmatter, never from a .bee/ store. An unresolvable --work id exits 1 with a typed unknown_work error.

work.description: The work item to assemble context for — matched against bee.id on a bee.work-item concept (the id is identity).

budget.description: Context budget in estimated tokens; sizes are bytes/4 (no tokenizer dependency). Explicit --budget always wins over --lane when both are given.

lane.description: Shorthand mapping to a lane-scaled budget preset (tiny 8000 / small 12000 / standard 20000 / high-risk 30000), resolved into --budget before this call reaches validate() — only when --budget is omitted. Omitting both --budget and --lane behaves exactly as before this option existed (required, missing).

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON ({work,decisions,budget,estimator,total_est,entries,truncated,excluded,floor,critical_total,zero_signal_count}) instead of the human table.

commands.name: knowledge.search
commands.description: Pull matching bee.pattern and bee.area concepts out of the bundle by symptom text — an error excerpt, a wrong-behavior description, a mechanism name — at any moment mid-flow. --text is required, whitespace-split into terms, lowercased, OR-matched by substring containment (the same rule `decisions search --text` uses). The corpus is patterns and areas ONLY: bee.decision concepts are `decisions search`'s (never double-reported), and the generated index.md/log.md files are never concepts to begin with. Matched fields are the concept title, its body (frontmatter stripped), and its frontmatter bee.sources/bee.decisions entries — where incident signatures and quoted error text usually live. Results are ranked deterministically: term-hit count descending, then the concept's own `timestamp` frontmatter field descending, then path ascending, so two runs over the same bundle are byte-identical. Each row is `path — title — why-matched`, where why-matched names every hit term and which field(s) it matched in — a result you can check, not a lucky guess. A zero-hit query is NOT an error: it returns an empty `results` array and a one-line note, exit 0 — a search miss is data mid-debug. Purely read-only: writes is always [], callable from any checkout at any phase.

text.description: Whitespace-separated search terms (case-insensitive, OR-matched by substring, ranked by hit count then recency). Required.

limit.description: Maximum result rows to return; a positive integer. Defaults to 5 — pass a larger value to widen, never to narrow below the default.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON ({text,results,count}) instead of one row per line.

commands.name: knowledge.promote
commands.description: Propose the knowledge a finished work item earned — and never write it. Resolves --work <id> to its bee.work-item concept, then READS the capped cell traces of that feature from .bee/cells/*.json (a read of the runtime store, which the bundle may perform; it is never a write path into one) and returns three PROPOSALS: (a) a DELIVERY DRAFT — a complete bee.delivery concept in canonical emitter form, ready to be saved as the work item's delivery.md sibling, carrying what shipped (each cell's recorded outcome), how it was verified (each cell's recorded verify command and evidence) and every recorded deviation; (b) AREA UPDATES — for each area named in the work item's bee.areas, the capped behavior_change cells whose files_changed touch that area's subject, as candidate spec-sync bullets each citing its cell id; (c) PATTERN CANDIDATES — every capped cell whose trace carries a deviation or a failure signature, shaped as a candidate bee.pattern concept with bee.polarity pitfall and bee.lifecycle draft, quoting the trace verbatim. Every proposed line traces to a cell trace or to the work item — nothing is invented. promote proposes and never writes — not into docs/knowledge/, not into .bee/*.json(l), not anywhere: `writes` in the --json payload is always []; applying a proposal is a human or agent decision. An unresolvable --work id exits 1 with a typed unknown_work error.

commands.description: Stand up docs/knowledge/ in a repo that has none yet, seeded from docs/specs/*.md: one bee.area concept per spec (title from its first ATX heading, description from the paragraph right after it, the spec body imported verbatim beneath fresh OKF frontmatter — id/lifecycle/areas/authoritative_for/sources), plus the generated index.md and subdir indexes via the same machinery `bee knowledge index` uses. No code scanning in v1 — specs-only import. Two typed refusals, both zero-write: `bundle_exists` when docs/knowledge/ already carries a concept (bootstrap never touches an existing bundle — use `bee knowledge check`/`bee knowledge index` on it instead), and `no_specs` when docs/specs/ is absent or holds no .md files. A spec bootstrap cannot classify (no derivable title, an empty or duplicate slug, or an unreadable file) is skipped and named as a gap rather than failing the whole run; the report names every area CREATED and every GAP so nothing silently vanishes.

commands.name: knowledge.report
commands.description: Read-only recurrence measurement over the bundle's bee.critical patterns. Per U8, an author may add a bee.signature to a critical bee.pattern concept — a deterministic, literally grep-able incident string. For every critical pattern that carries one, this counts the .bee/decisions.jsonl entries (decision/rationale/alternatives text) and .bee/capture-queue.jsonl stub entries (outcome/area/files text, flush rows excluded) whose text contains the signature as a LITERAL substring — never lowercased, never term-split, never OR-matched — AND whose own date is strictly after the pattern's timestamp (compared by calendar day; same-day entries do not count). Each measured pattern renders its recurrence count and last-seen date. A critical pattern with no bee.signature is listed under `unmeasured` and never guessed at. Purely read-only: no write ever reaches a pattern file or either log, callable from any checkout at any phase.

Must be run from the MAIN checkout (an ordinary, non-worktree directory), never from inside another linked worktree. Typed, zero-mutation refusal when the feature slug is invalid, --base-ref does not resolve to a commit, the target sibling path or branch already exists, or a grant already exists for the derived id; `git worktree add` failing at runtime is caught and re-surfaced typed too, and a failure AFTER the worktree was created rolls back best-effort. commands.name: worktree.merge
commands.description: Merge a granted worktree's branch back into the MAIN checkout — first a zero-mutation D7/D8 proof check: every capped cell for the merging feature must already carry a recorded proof line (“<command> — <result> — <scope reason>”, written by `bee cells finish --report`) — `bee worktree merge` never spawns commands.test itself. A capped cell whose report carries no valid proof line refuses the merge outright, naming the cell (WORKTREE_MERGE_PROOF_DEBT); a report-less legacy cap (pre-contract) passes ungated. This check runs before `git merge --no-ff <branch>` is ever attempted (run from MAIN once the check is green), so a proof debt never touches main. Must be run from the MAIN checkout (an ordinary, non-worktree directory) — running it from inside ANY linked worktree, including the one being merged, is refused (a worktree cannot merge itself). Typed, zero-mutation refusal when the id is unknown/ungranted, the MAIN or WORKTREE tree is dirty (a bootstrapped gitignored .bee store alone does not count as dirty), or the worktree is on a detached HEAD or a branch other than its expected `wt/<slug>`-style branch. Cleanup runs BY DEFAULT on a green (or skipped, loudly-warned) merge that actually merged something: `git worktree remove --force` (safe only because freshness was re-checked immediately before), `git branch -d` (never -D), then removeGrant — so a merged id never lingers in `bee worktree list` unless you ask it to. Pass `--no-cleanup` to opt ONE merge out, or set `.bee/config.json`'s `worktree_cleanup_on_merge` to `false` to opt a whole repo out; a non-boolean value on either is refused outright, never silently read as on. The legacy `--cleanup` flag is still accepted and validated but is now a no-op — cleanup-by-default replaced its old opt-in meaning, so passing it changes nothing. Cleanup never runs when the merge itself came back MERGE_CONFLICT or WORKTREE_MERGE_PROOF_DEBT, or when nothing was actually merged (an already-up-to-date branch removes nothing, flag or config notwithstanding). No flag needed for companion teardown: if the worktree was created `--with-companion`, its marker alone is enough — commands.worktree_companion_end runs and the mounted symlink is removed BEFORE the dirty-tree check, regardless of cleanup or how the merge itself resolves (an untracked companion symlink would otherwise read as a dirty worktree on every attempt). Queue-aware: every invocation enqueues through the shared integration queue (`controlRoot/.bee/runtime/integration/queue/`) and becomes the processor the instant the lease is free — an empty queue resolves immediately with the same output as an uncontended merge. A second concurrent merge against the same MAIN checkout waits its turn (bounded by --queue-wait-ms, default 180000) instead of racing the old dirty-tree refusal; on timeout the result is `ok:false, code:'INTEGRATION_QUEUE_TIMEOUT'` and the text unambiguously says the merge did NOT run, with the request's queue position — never a shape readable as success. uat-gate-before-merge D1: a standard/high-risk feature whose uat gate is not approved refuses the merge outright (zero-mutation, before the companion teardown) unless --skip-uat is passed for this one merge, or .bee/config.json uat_before_merge is set to false — the remedy names all three exits. Missing or unrecognized lane classification counts as standard (fails closed).

A non-boolean value (anything but a bare flag, `true`, or `false`) is refused outright, never silently read as either outcome. See also `.bee/config.json`'s `worktree_cleanup_on_merge` to opt a whole repo out.

Never combine with an auto-approval — the uat gate itself is never bypass-approved (see bee gate --name uat); this flag only skips the MERGE-TIME check, once, for this invocation. See also .bee/config.json config uat_before_merge (default true) to opt a whole repo out.

commands.name: worktree.prune
commands.description: Sweep DEAD worktrees the merge path never reclaimed: every worktree with a live grant or a .bee/runtime/workspaces/ record (a grantless orphan left by worktree unregister reaches this scan too) is removed only when its branch is fully merged into the MAIN checkouts own current branch (git merge-base --is-ancestor, exit-code only, never a parsed rev-list count, which reads any git failure as merged for every worktree at once), the tree holds no tracked-modified or untracked files and nothing precious ignored (a paused .bee/HANDOFF.json or a non-empty .bee/capture-queue.jsonl), no rebase/cherry-pick/merge/bisect is in progress, no session holds it with a heartbeat inside the liveness window, and its last commit is older than the age threshold. Every probe fails CLOSED: a missing record, an unreadable file, or a non-zero git exit keeps the worktree rather than removing it, and an unresolvable base ref refuses the whole run. Drops all four artifacts per dead worktree: directory (git worktree remove --force), branch (git branch -d, never -D), grant, workspace record, and prints one line per worktree naming why it was kept or removed; a removal line names the bytes reclaimed. Must be run from the MAIN checkout: it enumerates and removes OTHER worktrees, so a linked worktree cannot prune itself. Lock a worktree with git worktree lock <path> to opt it out permanently, git worktree remove --force refuses outright on a locked tree.

commands.description: The releasing door: on every invocation, releases every crashed-session claim the sweep's own criteria qualify (expired TTL, stale owner heartbeat, excluding the caller's own), marks every heartbeat-stale session record dead in place (cleared on that session's next heartbeat), and separately reports the crash candidates — sessions whose heartbeat is stale, whose transcript exists and lacks the clean-end trio, and that show a work signal (bound lane in a non-terminal phase, an active claimed cell, or transcript activity newer than the last durable settlement). No --release flag, no confirmation step. When it cannot resolve its own caller session it writes nothing — no release, no mark — and reports the counts it observed instead.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of the text report.

commands.name: recovery.window
commands.description: For one crash-candidate session id, re-derive the bounded mining window and the down-tier miner prompt: resolves the session's transcript, computes the window start from the last durable settlement (lane-scoped, global fallback, or the session's own started_at when nothing settled), applies the hard event cap, and returns {transcript, since_ts, event_count, window_truncated, prompt}. Never calls an LLM itself — the orchestrator dispatches the returned prompt to a down-tier worker.

session.description: The crash-candidate session id, from `recovery scan`.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of printing the prompt text.
