commands.name: dispatch.prepare
commands.description: Build a bee-owned dispatch payload (Agent tool / spawn_agent / an external cli executor) for the given runtime and purpose, plus an economics record (logical_tier, requested_model, channel, enforcement). kind "cell" resolves the generation tier for cell execution and requires --cell (loaded for prompt context) and --worker (checked against the cell's own status/claim owner); kinds "gather"/"reviewer" resolve read-only gather-shaped tiers (generation/review respectively); kind "advisor" resolves the configured advisor slot, never a bare tier. A cli-shaped resolution for kind "cell" is returned as a typed refusal ({ok:false, reason:"cli_tier_gather_only", ...}) — prepare never routes around it. For kind "cell", an unclaimed or foreign-claimed cell is refused as {ok:false, type:"refused", reason:"claim_ownership", code, status, owner, fix} naming the actual status/owner — --force-ownership overrides it and appends an audited ownership_override entry to the prepare-time dispatch record. A cli-shaped resolution for gather/reviewer/advisor builds an external-executor Bash payload instead of an Agent/spawn_agent one. Prompt wording lives in the vendored prompts/*.md files (rendered through the built-in prompt renderer); for kind "cell", the worker prompt conditionally gains two machine-assembled blocks — a compact "Prior rounds" digest when the cell record carries prior attempt history (blocks, tests-red finishes, deviations, judge consults, reopens), and a "Learned context" block of knowledge paths + one-line titles (never file contents; the cell's own read_first is never duplicated; every resolution failure silent) resolved from the knowledge-bundle work-item manifest, the bundle index pointer, or docs/history/learnings/critical-patterns.md — a first-dispatch cell in a repo with no knowledge layer renders byte-identically to before.

runtime.description: Target runtime the payload is shaped for.

cell.description: Cell id — required when --kind cell; loaded for prompt context.

worker.description: Requesting worker identity — required when --kind cell; checked against the cell's status/trace.worker (claim-ownership guard).

purpose.description: One-line statement of what a non-cell dispatch (gather/reviewer/advisor) is FOR. Folded into the dispatch label as "<kind>: <purpose>" on every transport (the claude Agent description, codex's task_name); ignored for --kind cell, whose label is always "<cell id>: <cell title>". Omitted, the label stays the bare kind — today's exact bytes.

force-ownership.description: Override a claim-ownership refusal for --kind cell (audited into the prepare-time dispatch record). Ignored for every other kind.

claim.description: One verb from "cell chosen" to "worker prompt in hand": claim the cell for --worker first (the same door as `cells claim` — refusals pass through unchanged), then reserve every path in the cell's files for that worker at the default TTL, then build the payload exactly as without the flag. On a reservation conflict the claim is unwound and the refusal names the conflicting paths and holder — state is left as it was found. The result gains {claimed: true, reserved: [paths]}. Only valid with --kind cell.

session-id.description: Session id the --claim claim is taken under (same optional/env-resolved convention as `cells claim`). Ignored without --claim.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of pretty-printed JSON (prepare always prints JSON; flag kept for surface consistency).

examples: bee dispatch prepare --runtime claude --kind cell --cell demo-1 --worker exec-demo-1 --json
bee dispatch prepare --runtime claude --kind cell --cell claim-demo-1 --worker exec-claim-demo --claim --json

commands.name: dispatch.wave
commands.description: Prepare cells of the CURRENT schedule wave (compute_schedule's first placed wave -- the same computation `cells schedule` reads) in one call: each cell runs through the identical claim+reserve+payload path `dispatch prepare --kind cell --claim` uses -- claim, reserve every declared file, build the dispatch envelope -- under an auto-derived worker nickname (`w-<cell id>`), so a payload in `wave` is byte-identical to what the single-cell command would have emitted for that cell. One cell's refusal never aborts the rest: a cell already claimed, or hitting a reservation conflict, lands in `skipped` as `{id, reason, detail}` (`already_claimed`, `reservation_conflict`, `claim_refused`, `prepare_failed`, `unwind_failed`, or `unsupported`) and the loop continues. `economics` carries one `{id, ...}` entry per cell that made it into `wave`. An empty wave (no schedulable cells, or every ready cell already claimed) returns every array empty rather than an absent/null key. This door MUTATES the shared control plane (claims, reservations, worker rows), so it always scopes to exactly ONE feature -- an explicit `--feature`, else the calling session's bound lane, else the default record's own `feature` (the same resolution every mutating `state` verb uses); nothing resolving is a typed refusal, never an every-feature grab. `--limit N` caps how many cells of the wave are actually claimed (the rest are left untouched, not reported); omitted, the whole wave stands.

runtime.description: Target runtime the payloads are shaped for.

feature.description: The one feature this wave scopes to. Omitted, resolved from the calling session's bound lane, then the default record's own `feature`; refused (typed) when none resolves.

limit.description: Maximum number of this wave's cells to actually claim; a positive integer. Omitted, the whole wave is claimed.

session-id.description: Session id every cell's claim in this wave is taken under (same optional/env-resolved convention as `cells claim` / `dispatch prepare --claim`).

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of pretty-printed JSON (wave always prints JSON; flag kept for surface consistency).

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Fail-closed runtime health report, a THREE-state verdict: overall_status is "blocked" when any mechanical row (hooks-file presence, capability-baseline byte match, hook-handler resolvability, skills-installed) is not ok; "degraded" when every mechanical row is ok but codex's hook-discovery/trust/project-trust/pending-review rows are still structurally unknown (per the capability matrix) and no valid attestation covers them; "ready" only with mechanical rows all ok AND, on codex, a currently-valid attestation (see "doctor attest") — claude has no trust-unknown rows, so mechanical green alone reaches ready there, no attestation required. Trust-row wording is version-scoped: a live codex --version other than the probed one reports "unprobed_version" instead of asserting the probed conclusions. Never "ready" from file presence alone. Performs zero writes anywhere, including the dispatcher's own pre-routing manifest-hash cache. PORTED 2026-08-02: the 'capability-baseline byte match' row named an artifact that no longer exists in the tree, so it is replaced by the byte match that does — the host's hook manifest against what this binary renders for that runtime. Same question, an artifact that exists, and it fails when it should.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a human-readable report.

commands.name: doctor.attest
commands.description: Record a static attestation that codex trust state was reviewed via the interactive /hooks TUI for THIS exact pairing of .codex/hooks.json content, codex --version, and repo identity. Written to the gitignored .bee/doctor-attest.json (never tracked state). "bee doctor --runtime codex" treats the attestation as valid only while all three legs still match the live state; any single drifted leg makes it inert and doctor reports "degraded" naming the stale reason (hash_changed / version_changed / identity_changed / no_attestation). --runtime codex only — claude has no trust-unknown rows to attest. No liveness leg exists: codex exposes no hook-fire event surface to observe, so this is a static record, not a health probe.

runtime.description: Must be "codex" — claude has no attestation model.

session.description: Optional session id to record alongside the attestation; defaults to $CODEX_SESSION_ID or $CLAUDE_SESSION_ID when unset.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a one-line confirmation.

commands.name: close
commands.description: Feature close driver — proof-checked: the one blocking door is TESTS, and it never spawns commands.test itself (D7, docs/history/test-doctrine/CONTEXT.md) — it reads whether every capped cell already carries a D8 proof line on its trace.report.tests ("<command> — <result> — <scope reason>", recorded by `bee cells finish --report`): green reports the remaining capture checklist (scribing/capture doors, report-only) and the next action; a capped cell whose report carries no valid proof line exits 1, naming the cell and the remedy — re-cap it with a real proof line, then re-run bee close. A capped cell with no report at all is legacy and passes ungated. --dry-run is a read-only report ({feature, doors:[{door, blocking, detail, command}]}) that runs nothing. Inside a granted worktree the text also names the merge-back road (bee worktree merge — which runs a zero-mutation D7/D8 proof check before `git merge --no-ff`, never commands.test). On a green close the feature's cells are RETIRED automatically: if every one of them is capped or dropped they move to .bee/cells/archive/<feature>/ and leave the hot scan path that `status` and `orient` parse on every call. A feature that closes green while still holding an open cell keeps its cells and close names the cell. Reverse with `bee cells unarchive --feature <f>`; opt a repo out with .bee/config.json `cells_archive_on_close: false`. After a GREEN, non-dry-run close, any dirty .bee/ bookkeeping (retirement, promote proposals) is auto-committed path-scoped to .bee — unrelated dirt and unrelated staged files are never swept, and a commit failure only warns (close stays green); opt a repo out with .bee/config.json `close_commit_bookkeeping: false`.

feature.description: Feature slug to drive toward close.

dry-run.description: Read-only: report the close doors and what settles each, without running anything.

json.description: Emit the machine-readable door report instead of the one-line-per-door text.

commands.name: test
commands.description: Run the project's ONE declared test path — .bee/config.json commands.test (a string or an array, run in order) — and write the normalized record .bee/logs/test-results.json: {ran_at, green, commands:[{command, exit, duration_ms, failure_excerpt, failure_log}]} where failure_excerpt is the last ≤500 chars of a failing command's output (null on pass). The runner is a program; an agent's word is never the record. A red run exits 1 but is a NORMAL result — the record is still written and the red is the next work item (`cells finish` refuses to cap on it). Text output is one ✓/✗ line per command ending in exactly one next: line. No commands.test declared: reports {green: null, undeclared: true} with how to declare it, runs nothing, exits 0.

json.description: Emit the machine-readable run record instead of the per-command text lines.

commands.name: onboard
commands.description: Install or upgrade bee in a target repository: the AGENTS.md BEE block (merged between BEE:START/END markers, never touching content outside them), the .bee/ runtime files, the vendored expertise layer, the hook wiring for each runtime, and the per-project skill projections. Idempotent and never destructive: existing state is preserved, and without --apply the call is a read-only PLAN — {status, changes_needed[], versions} — that mutates nothing. A `blocked_*` status means zero mutations happened and the reported `versions` explain why. This is the one maintenance surface every skill points at by name, and it is how a host repo gets the binary the hooks are wired to.

repo-root.description: Target repository root. Defaults to the current directory.

apply.description: Write the planned changes. Without it the call reports what WOULD change and touches nothing.

runtime.description: Which runtime projections to install: claude, codex, or both.

repo-hooks.description: Vendor the hook wiring into the repository.

plugin-source.description: Install from an unpacked plugin package rather than a source checkout.

claude-md.description: Write the CLAUDE.md import that loads the AGENTS.md block.

global-skills.description: Install the skills into the user-level skill directory instead of per-project.

force-downgrade.description: Permit installing an older bee over a newer one.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of the text form.

commands.name: rs-info
commands.description: Build identity for this binary: {runtime, ported[], fallback}. `fallback` is null since the R6 cutover — there is nothing behind the binary, so a shape it does not serve is refused rather than delegated. Read-only, needs no repo, and answers "which bee am I actually running" without touching any store.

commands.name: dev.render-skill-trees
commands.description: Regenerate the plugin skill projections (.claude-plugin/skills, .codex-plugin/skills) from skills/. Run it after ANY skill or reference edit — the projections are committed artifacts, and `bee onboard --apply` copies them, so a skipped render ships the previous wording. Source-checkout tool: it refuses outside a repo carrying both packages/bee/ and packages/bee-rs/.

commands.name: dev.render-prompt
commands.description: Render one of the vendored prompt files (packages/bee/prompts/*.md) with its placeholders filled, so a prompt change can be inspected before it reaches a worker. Every {{placeholder}} the template declares must be supplied; a missing one is a typed error, never a silently empty slot. Source-checkout tool.

var.description: A K=V placeholder binding. Repeatable, once per placeholder.

commands.name: dev.statusline
commands.description: Render the one-line bee status line for a host repo's terminal — the surface a runtime's statusLine setting invokes. Read-only, works in any onboarded repo (this is the one dev verb that is NOT source-checkout-only).

commands.name: dev.release-manifest
commands.description: Build, check or self-test the release manifest — the content hash of every file in bee's SHIPPED frame (the gitignored binary appears as a presence-only unhashed artifact). --check reports drift and is what CI runs; --write rewrites the stored manifest, which ADDING a shipped file requires before the rebuild-reproduces-the-committed-manifest test can pass again. Source-checkout tool.

check.description: Compare the tree against the stored manifest and report drift. Writes nothing.

write.description: Rewrite the stored manifest from the current tree.

selftest.description: Run the manifest builder's own consistency checks.

commands.name: dev.plugin-distribution
commands.description: The installers' distribution preflight: prove the client's installed bee plugin package matches the release manifest byte for byte, then plan (and with --apply, perform) the removal of the repo-local fallback copies it supersedes, so two copies of a skill can never disagree. Removal is a transaction — every target is renamed aside first and any failure renames all of them back. Reads a preflight snapshot of every target and revalidates it before touching anything, closing the TOCTOU window between plan and apply. This replaced the last helper script the installers shelled a Node runtime out for. Emits one JSON line; a refusal is {ok:false,status:"blocked",error} with exit 1.

mode.description: plugin-first (prove the package, plan the cleanup) or repo-copy (prove the plugin is NOT active, so onboarding may write repo copies). Required.

repo-root.description: The host repository whose fallback copies are in scope. Required.

release-manifest.description: Path to the release manifest whose package roles define the expected package inventory. Required.

plugin-state-file.description: JSON the installer captured from the client CLI describing its installed plugins, keyed by runtime. A leading UTF-8 BOM is tolerated (PowerShell 5.1 writes one). Required.

apply.description: Perform the planned removal. Without it the run is a dry run that writes nothing and reports what it would do.

codex-hybrid.description: Exempt .codex/hooks.json from the hook cleanup. Set on runs where onboarding just wrote the codex-hybrid hook projection — without it, this pass would strip the only mechanical enforcement Codex sessions get, immediately after the install reported success (GH #22 P0-1).

user-skill-root.description: A user-global skill root to clean, repeatable. Requires --ledger: only skills the ownership ledger names for that exact root are ever touched.

ledger.description: Ownership ledger (schemaVersion 1) naming which skills bee installed under each user-global root. Required whenever --user-skill-root is given.

commands.name: dev.install-support
commands.description: The installer's JSON steps, as verbs rather than inline interpreter one-liners: merge-plugin-state (two per-runtime plugin listings into one {claude,codex} document), plugin-installed (was bee installed for this runtime in the pre-run snapshot — prints 1/0, and 0 for every failure, since 'cannot tell' and 'was not' lead to the same safe rollback), field (one top-level field of a JSON document on stdin, or the literal parse_error), assert-parity (a bee status --json must show installed plus exact version equality and no non-extra drift), and assert-recheck (a fresh onboarding plan must be up_to_date, and names what is still outstanding when it is not). Reading these out of the shell is what let install.sh drop its last interpreter dependency; it also gave them somewhere to be tested, which as inline one-liners they never had.

claude.description: merge-plugin-state: the Claude CLI plugin listing.

codex.description: merge-plugin-state: the Codex CLI plugin listing.

out.description: merge-plugin-state: where to write the merged document.

key.description: field: the top-level key to print.

expect-version-from.description: assert-parity: a plugin.json whose version every projection must equal.

commands.name: dev.render-hook-manifests
commands.description: Regenerate the per-runtime hook manifests (packages/bee/hooks/*.json) that onboard wires into a host repo's settings. Run it after adding, removing or re-matching a hook — an unrendered manifest leaves the new hook unwired everywhere, which is a guard going quiet rather than red. Source-checkout tool.

commands.name: dev.regen
commands.description: Run the three-step regen chain in order — render-skill-trees, then onboard --repo-root . --apply, then release-manifest --write — stopping at the first red with that step named, one summary line per green step. One deterministic verb instead of sequencing the three by hand. Source-checkout tool: it refuses outside a repo carrying both packages/bee/ and packages/bee-rs/.

commands.name: herding.classify-lane
commands.description: Classify one PBI into its lane — {pbi, lane, hard_gate_flags[], lane_safe, reason} — the call the bee-herding cockpit makes before it will dispatch anything. An unknown PBI classifies as high-risk with lane_safe false: the failure direction is toward ceremony, never away from it.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of the text form.

commands.name: herding.interlock
commands.description: Report the dispatch loop's owner-enable interlock — {enabled, marker, main_root} — read before dispatch may build any dispatchable set. The main checkout root is resolved via `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`, so the answer is the same from inside any linked worktree; an unresolvable root reports `enabled:false` with its reason rather than assuming permission.

main-root.description: Resolve against this main checkout instead of discovering it from cwd.

commands.name: herding.command-template
commands.description: Print the cockpit's command template for a key — the exact shell line the control loop runs, kept in the binary so the shell scripts hold no command wording of their own.

main-root.description: Resolve against this main checkout instead of discovering it from cwd.

commands.name: herding.herdr-result
commands.description: Read a dotted path out of a herdr result document on stdin. Unparseable input is a typed error naming what it received — the control loop must never proceed on a value it failed to read.

context.description: Name used in the error line, so a failure says which read failed.

commands.name: herding.herdr-pane-id
commands.description: Resolve a cockpit pane id from its label, so the control loop addresses panes by name instead of by position.

commands.name: herding.wave
commands.description: The bee-side entry point (herding-orchestration D17) that turns herding.agent_command into a running wave. Reads herding.agent_command from <main-root>/.bee/config.json, splits token 0 into the herdr agent kind and the remaining tokens into the agent's own argv (D14), substitutes {MODEL} per token, and constructs the fleet crate's HerdrBackend with them — an unrecognised token 0 is a typed error naming the herding.agent_command key, never a generic start failure. Worker specs (name, task, and an optional worktree recorded alongside the row) are read as JSON on stdin: a bare array, or {"workers": [...]}. Runs the fleet choreography and appends exactly one row to the wave ledger (.bee/wave-ledger.jsonl, D10).

main-root.description: Resolve against this main checkout instead of discovering it from cwd.

wave-id.description: The wave ledger row's wave_id. Defaults to a timestamp-based id.

worker-settle-ms.description: Wall-clock ceiling, in milliseconds, the choreography waits for one worker to settle. Default 60000.

poll-interval-ms.description: How often, in milliseconds, the choreography re-reads a worker's status while waiting. Default 500.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a one-line summary.

commands.name: herding.occupancy
commands.description: The CLI bridge to the wave ledger's read side (herding-orchestration D10), reachable from a markdown role for the first time — role-dispatch.md §4 can only run shell commands, and the ledger's read side was crate-private. Reports how many worker slots are occupied right now AND which answer it gave: a real cross-check against herdr's own live pane list ("live") when `herdr pane list` succeeds, or the degraded one-hour timer fallback ("fallback") when it does not — the two never collapse into one bare count.

main-root.description: Resolve against this main checkout instead of discovering it from cwd.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a one-line summary.

commands.name: herding.record-worker
commands.description: The recording verb (herding-orchestration D18) role-dispatch.md §8 calls immediately after a successful `herdr agent start`, so the spawn it just made is visible to the very next iteration's `bee herding occupancy` read. Appends exactly one row to the wave ledger (.bee/wave-ledger.jsonl, D10) through the SAME append path `bee herding wave` uses — no second write path, the file stays append-only. The row carries one worker with outcome left unset (null): dispatch spawns and walks away, it never learns an outcome itself. `wave-id` defaults to the worker's own `name` when not given, so a later caller that already knows the same slug can append a resolved row under the identical wave_id and supersede this one at read time (wave_ledger::fold_waves_by_wave_id), never by rewriting these bytes. A spawn this verb is never called for is invisible to the next occupancy read — the whole reason it exists.

main-root.description: Resolve against this main checkout instead of discovering it from cwd.

name.description: The spawned worker's own self-chosen slug/label.

pane-id.description: The herdr pane id the worker is running in.

path.description: The worktree path the worker was given, recorded alongside the row.

task.description: The item the worker was given, e.g. a PBI id.

wave-id.description: The wave ledger row's wave_id. Defaults to the worker's own --name.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a one-line confirmation.

commands.name: staging.add
commands.description: Merge a feature's branch into the staging mixing-ground (staging-lane D0/D0a): lazily creates the "staging" branch and its sibling worktree (../<repo-basename>--wt--staging) from CURRENT main the first time this runs — never from a feature branch — then resolves --feature's branch (a registered worktree's creation identity, falling back to the "wt/<slug>" convention) and merges it into staging with `git merge --no-ff`. A textual conflict aborts the merge (`git merge --abort`) and reports it typed (STAGING_MERGE_CONFLICT, naming the feature and the conflicting files) — the staged set is left unchanged and staging stays usable for the next feature. On a clean merge the feature is upserted into `.bee/runtime/staging.json`'s `staged[]` (feature, branch, last_merged_sha, at); re-running `add` for the same feature later re-merges (git only replays the new commits) and updates last_merged_sha. Then runs the project's configured commands.staging_build (if any) inside the staging worktree — a non-zero exit is a typed STAGING_BUILD_FAILED error carrying the tail of its output; when commands.staging_build is not configured, the build step is skipped with a visible note, never silently. Must be run from the MAIN checkout (an ordinary, non-worktree directory) — staging is lazily created FROM MAIN and can only ever be triggered from there.

feature.description: The feature slug to merge into staging — resolved to its branch via a registered worktree's creation identity, or the "wt/<slug>" convention.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a short confirmation report.

commands.name: staging.rebuild
commands.description: D0a trigger 3: re-derive the staging invariant (staging = main + Σ features awaiting UAT). Runs `git reset --hard main` in the staging worktree, then recomputes the awaiting-UAT subset of `.bee/runtime/staging.json`'s `staged[]` — a feature whose uat gate reads "approved" on its own workflow record (read from the MAIN root), or whose branch no longer exists, DROPS OUT automatically; missing/unreadable workflow-record state fails toward keeping the feature staged. Every remaining feature is re-merged with `git merge --no-ff`, in staged order, except any named in --without (which stay members of the staged set but are skipped THIS run). A merge conflict aborts just that one merge (`git merge --abort`), is reported typed (STAGING_MERGE_CONFLICT, naming the feature and files) and leaves the feature staged at its last successful merge — one broken feature never blocks re-merging the rest. `base_sha` is updated to main's current commit, then the project's configured commands.staging_build (if any) runs in the staging worktree, same as `staging add`. Must be run from the MAIN checkout; refuses typed (STAGING_NO_RECORD) when no staging record exists yet.

without.description: Comma-separated feature slugs to keep staged but skip merging this run (e.g. "a,b").

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a short confirmation report.

commands.name: staging.status
commands.description: Zero-mutation snapshot of the staging mixing-ground: the current `staged[]` set from `.bee/runtime/staging.json`, each feature's uat gate state ("approved"/"pending"/"unknown", read from its own workflow record on the MAIN root), and a stale-base warning when staging's recorded `base_sha` no longer matches main's current commit — the D0a trigger-3 reminder to run `bee staging rebuild`. Never runs `git reset`, `git merge`, or writes the staging record. Reports `exists:false` (never an error) when no staging record exists yet — `staging status` is a plain query, not a refusal path.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a short text report.

commands.name: discovery.list
commands.description: Scan every discovery effort under docs/discovery/ and report each MAP.md's Destination line plus two ticket counts: open (status: open) and frontier (open, unclaimed, and every blocked-by target closed). An unreadable MAP.md never crashes the scan — it surfaces as a visible "unreadable <path> — remedy: fix or delete" line instead.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of the formatted list.

commands.name: discovery.stub
commands.description: Create a new MAP.md for a discovery effort whose destination is not yet known, seeding it with the --from text under Notes. Refuses, writing nothing, when the --effort slug already has a directory under docs/discovery/ — resuming an existing map is a different operation from charting a new one.

effort.description: Lowercase kebab-case slug for the new discovery effort; becomes its directory name under docs/discovery/.

from.description: Prose context seeded into the new MAP.md's Notes section — e.g. why this effort was parked.

json.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a one-line confirmation.

examples: bee discovery stub --effort onboarding-flow --from "parked from route Qualify: too vague" --json
